items.followUp: Name two enzymes used in biological detergents and state the stains each removes.

rubric.why: Proteases break down proteins in stains such as blood or egg.
rubric.description: Names protease and links it to removing protein stains.
rubric.how: Award for the correct protease–protein stain pairing.

rubric.why: Lipases break down fats and oils.
rubric.description: Names lipase and links it to removing fat or oil stains.
rubric.how: Award for the correct lipase–fat or oil stain pairing.

modelAnswer: Proteases in biological detergents break down protein stains such as blood or egg.
Lipases break down fat and oil stains.

items.followUp: Define aerobic respiration and write its balanced chemical equation.

rubric.why: Aerobic respiration breaks down glucose in the presence of oxygen and releases energy.
rubric.description: Defines aerobic respiration by stating what is broken down, the role of oxygen, and the release of energy.
rubric.how: Award for a definition containing glucose breakdown, oxygen, and energy release.

rubric.why: The balanced equation shows glucose and oxygen producing carbon dioxide, water, and energy.
rubric.description: Writes the balanced chemical equation or the correct word equation for aerobic respiration.
rubric.how: Award for the balanced chemical equation or a complete, correct word equation.

modelAnswer: Aerobic respiration is the breakdown of glucose in the presence of oxygen to release energy.

items.followUp: Describe how temperature and substrate concentration affect the rate of enzyme action.

rubric.why: Rising temperature increases enzyme activity up to the optimum temperature.
rubric.description: Explains that enzyme activity increases as temperature rises up to an optimum.
rubric.how: Award for stating that increasing temperature raises activity up to the optimum.

rubric.why: Above the optimum, enzymes denature and their activity falls.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of temperatures above the optimum.
rubric.how: Award for stating that high temperature causes denaturation or a fall in enzyme activity.

rubric.why: Increasing substrate concentration increases the reaction rate while enzyme active sites are available.
rubric.description: Explains that adding substrate increases the reaction rate while active sites are available.
rubric.how: Award for linking increased substrate concentration to an increased reaction rate.

rubric.why: The rate levels off when all enzyme active sites are occupied and the enzymes are saturated.
rubric.description: Explains why the reaction rate eventually stops increasing with substrate concentration.
rubric.how: Award for stating that active sites become occupied and the rate levels off.

modelAnswer: As temperature rises, enzyme activity increases until it reaches an optimum temperature.
Above the optimum, the enzyme denatures and its activity falls; low temperatures slow the reaction.
As substrate concentration increases, the reaction rate increases while enzyme active sites are available.
The rate eventually levels off when all active sites are occupied and the enzymes are saturated.
